Maya / Samir,

Following up on our Q3 readout — attaching the token-level usage export and a short sample of latency traces for heavy inference windows (attachments: usage_report_Q3.csv, latency_sample.log). High level summary: 

- Token spend: BrightPath is trending +86% YoY for inference tokens; 70% of traffic is production scoring (low-latency) and 30% is experimental batch jobs.
- Peak concurrency: sustained spikes at 120 concurrent requests between 10:00–11:30 PT on weekdays (samples included).
- Unit economics: current pay-as-you-go suggests unit cost will increase ~28% over next 6 months at projected volume.

We ran Redwood Optimize over your trace and have three concrete levers: prefix caching for the scoring pipeline, model quantization on experimental jobs, and a stepped commit that smooths burst capacity. The attached mutual_action_plan.docx (draft) outlines a recommended 12‑month commit split (60% baseline commit, 40% burst credits).

Proposal ask:
- 12‑month term starting 2027-01-01
- Baseline commit: 1.5B tokens / month (covers steady scoring)
- Burst credits: additional 600M tokens / month available at pre-agreed uplift rate
- SLA: 95th pctl latency target for scoring routes; Redwood to provide telemetry dashboards and token-level cost breakdowns weekly during onboarding.

Next steps: If this aligns, can we schedule a 30‑minute call to review pricing and the mutual action plan? cc’ing Karthik (pricing) and Monica (ops) to confirm feasibility on our side.

Thanks,

Looping internal ops/pricing notes here so we can respond with concrete numbers. Notes from analysis: 

- Hourly p95 request latency: ops exported last 30 days; median p95 for scoring route is 210ms, tail episodically up to 520ms during sustained concurrency >100. We can provide per-hour p95 CSV for Dec.
- Pricing baseline: current PAYG blended effective price (BrightPath) ~ $38 / 1M tokens. Proposed committed pricing (1.5B baseline + 40% burst) effective blended rate ~= $27 / 1M tokens assuming standard 12‑month discount tiers and 60% utilization of burst.
- True-ups: standard quarterly true-up with overage billed at pre-negotiated burst uplift (15% over baseline rate). We can add a cap clause for year 1 to limit unexpected bill shock (suggested cap: 25% quarterly over baseline).
- Tech levers: enabling prefix cache for scoring alone projected to reduce token chargeable work by ~12% (savings applied immediately). Experimental job quantization yields ~2–3x inference speedup but requires a brief validation window.

Recommended reply to BrightPath: share per-hour p95 export, present blended pricing table and commit schedule, include optional cap clause and next call times. I can draft a pricing appendix for the mutual action plan if you want.
